answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with quadratic stake: each identity locks real collateral, yet voting weight rises only as the square root of that stake, so splitting one purse into many hollow aliases buys no extra influence. Honest attestations stack into a trust mesa, and every newcomer posts an umber bond that is slashed if they double-vote. To buy k votes an attacker must pledge k squared collateral, and any detected fraud burns it all, so the cost always outruns the reward.
